context.exploration_scope: Judged PHASE-SSI-S3's sole PROMOTION_CANDIDATE_ONLY signal for real adoption: re-derived its evidence fresh, re-ran the E12/E23/E33/S-series duplication/conflict check, and ran a mechanical scope-boundedness check to confirm the draft principle statement claims nothing beyond its 3 real evidence records

problem: PHASE-SSI-S3 recorded sig_goal_production_runtime_successful_resolution as a promotion candidate with a draft principle statement, but never checked whether that statement's generalization claims (across action types and phases) stayed within what its 3 evidence records actually support, or whether adopting it now would still be evidentially and non-conflictingly sound.

decision.decision_summary: 1 PROMOTION_CANDIDATE_ONLY signal(s) from S3 judged for adoption. 1 passed fresh evidence re-derivation, non-duplication/non-conflict, and scope-boundedness re-verification: sig_goal_production_runtime_successful_resolution, recorded as PROMOTED_PRINCIPLE_RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED. 0 rejected on recheck. 0 automatic policy adoption, 0 CI wiring, 0 automatic execution, 0 real project modifications. Verdict: PROMOTED_PRINCIPLE_RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED.

action.action_summary: Re-derived each PROMOTION_CANDIDATE_ONLY signal's evidence directly from the canonical Experience Layer, re-ran the E12/E23/E33+S-series duplication/conflict check, and mechanically verified the draft principle statement's generalization claims (action-type count, phase count, and absence of unbounded quantifiers) match what the freshly re-derived evidence actually supports before recording adoption.

result.note: 1 principle(s) adopted as PROMOTED_PRINCIPLE_RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED -- recorded, but not CI-linked, not auto-policy-applied, not auto-executed.

cause.root_cause_summary: A promotion candidate can pass every duplication and generalizability check from the prior phase and still overclaim at adoption time if its statement text was never checked word-for-word against what the underlying evidence count actually supports -- scope-boundedness has to be its own explicit, mechanical check at the moment of adoption, not assumed from an earlier generalizability pass.

lesson: Adopting a principle is the point where overclaiming becomes cheapest and most dangerous -- checking the adopted statement text itself (not just its underlying member count) against the freshly re-derived evidence, and recording the result as explicitly not-enforced, keeps a real adoption honest without silently becoming a binding rule.
